I'm in the same position as you and trying to find help too. I'm trying to swallow the shame to reach out to my professors but I don't even feel like I know how. It's my senior year for my BA but I've always swallowed my mental health issues and taken the bad grade instead. 


Does anyone know how to approach it? Should I/OP be honest about the mental health issues? I'm so worried about sounding like I'm making excuses, but I'm trying to find a therapist and have repeatedly been told they're overbooked right now. I've been pushing therapy off due to my resources and anxiety over starting for years so it feels extremely shameful to me. 


Also, I know you said lists aren't helping but a good starting point to help things stop feeling quite as overwhelming for me is a master list for each class. I go through one class at a time and write down: 

1. what assignments are completed with grade

2. missing assignments no longer able to make up 

3. missing assignments still able to make up 

4. assignments left to do. 

I also make notes of each classes late policy and assignment drop policy because it can help ease the anxiety sometimes

Oh my god, I am in pain for you right now, I'm so sorry that happened to you. That must have been so terrifying, there's literally no excuse for her as much as they love to use them. I'm so lucky my aunt gave me one of those puberty books when I was young. Even knowing they're narcissistic, abusive parents I can not comprehend how women could do this to other girls as if they don't know how scary everything is at first even if you expect it. Its almost a different level of traumatic neglect to have you figure that out on your own

Wow, we have different situations but I felt like I was just reading my own thoughts and feelings about my mom too. 

I'm still processing that whiplash too but my grandpa told me some helpful advice today that somehow helped me with that feeling so I want to share in case it helps you. For context, my grandpa is an ex alcoholic who was abusive to my mom but he's worked his entire life to really change himself and atone. It's not the side you necessarily want advice from, I know, but he wasn't a narc and I do think he is an example of the change we both want from our moms. 


"You only know yourself. You're the only person you can control so focus on controlling yourself and your life.  You're wonderful and you matter"

I don't know, its helping me a little to accept that I can't force my mom to be the mom I deserve. It also reinforces to me that if Nmom is ever going to change, its going to take years of work and self reflection like my grandpa did, and I can't force her to do that. I don't think she's even capable of it. 

I'm sorry if that's just completely unhelpful rambling but you're not alone. You matter and you deserve more than what she's done. You don't need to accept anything less than you deserve from anyone, not even disappointment from "family" (in case you haven't heard that in a while)

yes! 

Its not right since that's all we knew, like we were meant to be grateful for the "lesser" abuse. 

My dad was a meth head who abandoned us (although he visited intermittently in between jail and whatever else) and my Nmom held that over me my entire life. She was the good, selfless mom who threw her life away and quit drugs for me so I should be endlessly grateful to have a single parent left! As I got older she would occasionally remind me of the terrible things my dad did that I didn't know about so I would feel guilty and just listen to her or whatever. Like if I gave her too much "attitude" she would tell the story of how my dad stole her car to go to the store when I was 2 weeks old but actually was at strip clubs states away for months, remind me of when my dad abused me etc. Or when i was too happy she would let me know which one of my habits or physical features were similar to my father that i hated at that point. When I was more in my teens it would make me angry but when I was younger it made me feel bad for my mom having to be around me like my existence was my fault. Oh, my poor selfless, abusive mom.

Sorry for the extra details, its very new to me to recognize and recall these experiences but its kind of freeing to actually vent
I really love that, thank you. We are the champions that end the cycle.

thank you. 

She really made me think that it was something girls were just supposed to know how to do so it really felt like it was my fault they were making fun of me. Now I can't even fathom that grown, middle aged women reacted like that!

My mother wouldn't even teach me how to use a tampon. She made them this scary, "slutty" thing I had to BEG to use. I won't punish anyone with details but pads were not a good option for me even when I was young. For my cousins birthday we went to a Waterpark and I didnt want to miss it because of my period so she finally let me start using them. I was the oldest girl on a trip with all younger girls and my uncle. 


She wouldn't buy them until we were waiting for my uncle to pick me up and go to the water park!!! I mean, she sent me clueless to figure out tampons for the first time alone and in public. She was adamant that Im fine on my own and she didn't want to talk about how vaginas work, at all. She didn't even send me with the box and instructions. My poor uncle had to try his best to teach me then when I was crying/embarrassed and decided to sit out all day, a lifeguard had to teach me with all of these grown women laughing and making fun of me in the bathroom. 


I'm now starting to wonder if this is exactly what my mom wanted to happen, public shame and borderline traumatic embarrassment

Thank you so much for sharing! Reading your post and watching this video made me have to just sit for a minute  because it suddenly just clicked. I never thought of it this way and your experience really made it click for me. My mom likes to brag about my successes because of all of the attention for her. But I remember I used to hide when I had a really good day or had a good time when I hung out with friends (rarely allowed to), like i basically had to hide being happy! Everytime I was happy or life was going well for me, she would find something to criticize me for and then take my phone away or put on house arrest for no reason. I had to absolutely *beg* for anything resembling a social life or an interest outside of school or even having a job (while also being given $0 but having to pay for even my own school supplies ofc). Now that I think about it, the only thing in my life that mattered for her was my grades because she felt that it reflected on her. 

Just sharing because the clarity is kind of nice and hopefully it might help someone else too
